events.title: Ban Chiang Culture
events.description: Archaeological sites in the Ban Chiang area of northeastern Thailand reveal prehistoric culture with bronze and pottery-making technology. Ban Chiang culture is one of Southeast Asia's earliest bronze civilizations, significant for studying Southeast Asian prehistory.

events.title: Dvaravati Kingdom Period
events.description: Dvaravati was a Mon kingdom in central Thailand that practiced Theravada Buddhism. This period saw Buddhism taking root in Thailand, profoundly influencing later Thai culture.

events.title: Khmer Empire Influence
events.description: The Angkor Dynasty (Khmer Empire) ruled northeastern and central Thailand. Khmer culture, architecture, and administrative systems significantly influenced Thailand, with many Khmer-style temple ruins preserved today.

events.title: Sukhothai Kingdom Founded
events.description: The Sukhothai Kingdom was established, marking the first unified Thai kingdom. Sukhothai means 'Dawn of Happiness,' and this period is considered the golden age of Thai culture.

events.title: King Ramkhamhaeng Creates Thai Script
events.description: King Ramkhamhaeng the Great of Sukhothai created the Thai alphabet system (based on Khmer script). The creation of Thai script was a milestone in Thai cultural development, giving the Thai people their own written language.

events.title: Ayutthaya Kingdom Founded
events.description: King U Thong established the Ayutthaya Kingdom with Ayutthaya as capital. This kingdom lasted 417 years, becoming one of Southeast Asia's most powerful kingdoms, trading with China, Japan, and Europe.

events.title: Portuguese Arrive
events.description: The Portuguese first arrived at Ayutthaya and began trading with Thailand. This marked the beginning of Thailand's direct contact with Europe.

events.title: Yamada Nagamasa in Ayutthaya
events.description: Japanese samurai Yamada Nagamasa held important positions in Ayutthaya, leading the Japanese community. This period saw close Thai-Japanese relations, with many Japanese merchants and adventurers active in Thailand.

events.title: Fall of Ayutthaya
events.description: Burmese forces captured and destroyed Ayutthaya, ending the kingdom. Many cultural treasures and historical documents were destroyed, marking a major disaster in Thai history.

events.title: King Taksin Rebuilds Nation
events.description: King Taksin (of Chinese descent) expelled Burmese forces and established the Thonburi Dynasty with Thonburi (opposite Bangkok) as capital. Taksin quickly reunified Thailand and rebuilt the nation.

events.title: Chakri Dynasty (Rama Dynasty) Founded
events.description: Chao Phraya Chakri (Rama I) established the Chakri Dynasty (current dynasty) with Bangkok as capital. This dynasty continues to the present, with the current king being Rama X.

events.title: Burney Treaty
events.description: Thailand signed the Burney Treaty with Britain, beginning formal diplomatic relations with the West. This was an important step in Thailand's modernization.

events.title: Reign of Rama IV (King Mongkut)
events.description: Rama IV promoted modernization reforms, learning Western science and technology while protecting Thai sovereignty. The film 'The King and I' is set during this period, though with many inaccuracies.

events.title: Bowring Treaty
events.description: Thailand signed the Bowring Treaty with Britain, opening more trade privileges. Though an unequal treaty, it helped Thailand avoid becoming a colony.

events.title: Reign of Rama V (King Chulalongkorn)
events.description: King Chulalongkorn the Great implemented comprehensive modernization reforms, abolished slavery, and established modern administrative, educational, judicial, and military systems. Successfully maintaining Thai independence amid British and French colonial expansion, he is revered as one of Thailand's greatest kings.

events.title: Franco-Thai Crisis
events.description: French gunboats threatened Bangkok, forcing Thailand to cede territories east of the Mekong River (present-day Laos) to French Indochina. Thailand lost vast territories but maintained independence in core areas.

events.title: Bangkok Treaty
events.description: Thailand signed the Bangkok Treaty with Britain, ceding four sultanates in southern Malay Peninsula to Britain (now part of Malaysia). This was a territorial sacrifice Thailand made to maintain independence.

events.title: Joins World War I
events.description: Thailand declared war on the Central Powers, sending troops to participate in WWI. After the war, as a victor nation, Thailand abolished unequal treaties with Western powers.

events.title: Constitutional Revolution
events.description: The People's Party launched a bloodless coup, ending absolute monarchy and establishing constitutional monarchy. This was a major transformation in Thailand's political system, with the king becoming a symbolic head of state.

events.title: Siam Renamed Thailand
events.description: The Phibun government changed the country's name from 'Siam' to 'Thailand,' meaning 'Land of the Free,' emphasizing Thai ethnic identity and national sovereignty.

events.title: World War II Period
events.description: After Japanese invasion, Thailand was forced to ally with Japan and declare war on Britain and the US. However, the underground 'Free Thai Movement' secretly cooperated with the Allies. After the war, Thailand avoided being treated as a defeated nation.

events.title: Mysterious Death of Rama VIII
events.description: Young King Rama VIII (Ananda Mahidol) died mysteriously in the palace, officially declared an accident, but the truth remains a mystery. His brother Bhumibol succeeded as Rama IX.

events.title: Rama IX (Bhumibol) Ascends Throne
events.description: Bhumibol Adulyadej ascended as Rama IX, beginning a 70-year reign (1946-2016), becoming one of the world's longest-reigning monarchs. He was deeply beloved by the Thai people and made significant contributions to national development.

events.title: Phibun Returns to Power
events.description: Phibun regained power through a coup, implementing authoritarian rule. He pursued anti-communist policies and strengthened alliance with the United States.

events.title: Marshal Sarit Period
events.description: Marshal Sarit Thanarat came to power through a coup and promoted economic development policies. He emphasized traditional Thai values and maintained pro-US, anti-communist foreign policy.

events.title: Beginning of Rapid Economic Development
events.description: Thailand's economy began rapid development, with accelerated industrialization and modernization. Bangkok quickly developed into an international metropolis, and tourism began to rise.

events.title: Thailand's Role During Vietnam War
events.description: During the Vietnam War, Thailand allowed US forces to use Thai air bases and sent troops to support South Vietnam. Thai-US relations peaked, with Thailand's economy benefiting from US military spending.

events.title: October 14 Incident
events.description: Students and citizens launched massive pro-democracy demonstrations, overthrowing the Thanom military dictatorship. This was an important democratic movement in Thai history, opening a brief democratic period.

events.title: Thammasat University Massacre
events.description: Military police and right-wing groups bloodily suppressed students at Thammasat University, causing dozens of deaths. The military then staged another coup, democracy regressed, and leftist students were forced to flee to the jungle.

events.title: Prem Tinsulanonda in Power
events.description: General Prem Tinsulanonda became Prime Minister, promoting democratization and economic liberalization policies. This period saw sustained high economic growth and relative political stability.

events.title: Economic Miracle Period
events.description: Thailand's economy grew at 8-13% annually, earning it recognition as one of the 'Four Asian Tigers.' Manufacturing and exports developed rapidly, with massive foreign investment flowing in.

events.title: Black May Incident
events.description: Citizens protested against military-born Suchinda becoming Prime Minister, launching massive demonstrations. The military opened fire, causing severe casualties. The King intervened to mediate, forcing Suchinda to resign and promoting Thai democratization.

events.title: Asian Financial Crisis Begins
events.description: The Thai baht collapsed, triggering the Asian Financial Crisis in Thailand that rapidly spread across Asia. Thailand's economy severely contracted, requiring IMF assistance. The crisis exposed structural problems in the Thai economy.

events.title: New Constitution Promulgated
events.description: Thailand promulgated a new constitution called the 'People's Constitution,' expanding democratic rights and strengthening human rights protections. This constitution is considered the most democratic in Thai history.

events.title: Thaksin Elected Prime Minister
events.description: Telecommunications tycoon Thaksin Shinawatra led the Thai Rak Thai Party to electoral victory, becoming Prime Minister. He implemented populist policies, gaining rural and lower-class support, but triggering opposition from urban middle class and traditional elites.

events.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
events.description: The Indian Ocean tsunami struck Thailand's southern coast, especially tourist destinations like Phuket, causing thousands of deaths including many foreign tourists. This was one of the worst natural disasters in Thai history.

events.title: Military Coup Ousts Thaksin
events.description: The military launched a coup while Thaksin was visiting New York, overthrowing the elected government. The coup triggered long-term political turmoil in Thailand, intensifying Red Shirt and Yellow Shirt opposition.

events.title: Yellow Shirts Occupy Airports
events.description: The anti-Thaksin People's Alliance for Democracy (Yellow Shirts) occupied Bangkok's two major airports, paralyzing transport. The political crisis deepened, with two pro-Thaksin prime ministers, Samak and Somchai, successively removed from office.

events.title: Red Shirt Protests and Crackdown
events.description: Pro-Thaksin United Front for Democracy Against Dictatorship (Red Shirts) launched massive protests in Bangkok, occupying commercial districts. Military forces violently suppressed the protests, causing over 90 deaths and hundreds of injuries.

events.title: Yingluck Elected Prime Minister
events.description: Thaksin's younger sister Yingluck Shinawatra was elected Prime Minister, becoming Thailand's first female PM. Her government faced continuous political confrontation.

events.title: Massive Anti-Government Protests
events.description: Opposition launched massive demonstrations demanding Yingluck's resignation. Protesters occupied government departments and major intersections, plunging Thailand into serious political crisis.

events.title: Military Coup
events.description: Army Commander General Prayuth Chan-ocha launched a coup, overthrowing Yingluck's government and establishing military rule (National Council for Peace and Order). Thai democracy was interrupted again.

events.title: Death of Rama IX
events.description: King Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama IX), who reigned for 70 years, passed away, plunging the nation into mourning. He was one of the world's longest-reigning monarchs, deeply beloved by the Thai people. His son Vajiralongkorn succeeded as Rama X.

events.title: State Funeral of Rama IX
events.description: Thailand held a grand cremation ceremony for King Rama IX, with hundreds of thousands participating in mourning. The entire nation entered a one-year mourning period.

events.title: First Election After Military Rule
events.description: Thailand held its first election after the coup, but the electoral system favored the military. Prayuth was controversially elected Prime Minister and continued in power. The new Future Forward Party gained massive youth support.

events.title: Youth Democracy Movement
events.description: Young people launched a massive democracy movement demanding constitutional reform, the Prime Minister's resignation, and unprecedentedly calling openly for monarchy reform. The movement used innovative protest forms, gaining international attention.

events.title: COVID-19 Response
events.description: Thailand implemented preventive measures to combat COVID-19. The pandemic severely impacted Thailand's tourism-dependent economy, with rising unemployment and slow economic recovery.

events.title: Move Forward Party Wins Election
events.description: The progressive Move Forward Party won the most seats in elections, with 42-year-old leader Pita gaining strong youth support. However, due to political obstacles, Move Forward Party failed to form government.

events.title: Srettha Becomes Prime Minister
events.description: Pheu Thai Party candidate Srettha Thavisin was elected Prime Minister in parliamentary vote. Srettha is a real estate tycoon who promised to promote economic recovery and social reconciliation.
